text:
acme-admin: Hey team — our users started getting SSO errors after our IdP rotated certs overnight. Immediate failures on login, error in browser: "SAML Response validation failed: InvalidSignature". Ticket STR-1824. Can someone help triage?

maria.chen: Sorry to hear that — sending to eng-security. Do you have the IdP metadata XML and the exact ACS (Assertion Consumer Service) URL you're sending in the IdP config? Also any SAMLResponse logs (base64 blob) would help.

acme-admin: Here's what our admin uploaded as IdP metadata (redacted):
```xml
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.acme-corp.com">
  <IDPSSODescriptor>
    <SingleSignOnService Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-Redirect" Location="https://idp.acme-corp.com/sso"/>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <KeyInfo><X509Data><X509Certificate>MIIC...REDACTED...AB</X509Certificate></X509Data></KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```
Our ACS URL in the IdP is set to: https://console.redwoodinference.com/saml/consume
We saw this in the browser console: "Destination mismatch: expected https://console.redwood.ai/sso/acs"

maria.chen: Aha — that Destination mismatch is a clear sign ACS URL/entityID mismatch. Our product expects the ACS URL to be https://console.redwood.ai/sso/acs for that org by default. Did your admin update a custom ACS?

acme-admin: We thought the new ACS was https://console.redwoodinference.com/saml/consume because that was shown in a previous copy of the metadata. We didn't change anything else during cert rotation.

jack.wong: Two parallel things here: 1) Destination/ACS mismatch (fixable by updating IdP to use the exact ACS we expect or adding the alternate ACS via customer config if available). 2) InvalidSignature — usually indicates either the IdP cert in metadata doesn't match the cert used to sign the SAMLResponse, or the cert wasn't uploaded correctly (truncated/line break issue). Please grab the actual SAMLResponse (base64) from the browser POST to the ACS and paste it here (redact user PII). Also include any error snippets from our SAML assertion validator (we log signature validation and fingerprint).

acme-admin: Pasting redacted SAMLResponse base64 (first 200 chars): 
```nPD94bWwgdmVyc2lvbj0iMS4wIj8+PHNhbWxwOlJlc3BvbnNlIHhtbG5zOnNhbWxwPSJ1cm46b2FzaXM6bmFtZXM6dGM6U0FNTDoyLjAi
```

samir.patel: Jack and Maria — while they pull the full SAMLResponse, two quick checks: 1) certificate fingerprint mismatch — ask them to compute SHA1 fingerprint of the cert they uploaded. 2) clock skew: SAML assertions are time-sensitive; confirm both IdP and SP clocks within ~60s. Also, did the IdP rotate certs AND change metadata URL? Sometimes rotation publishes new metadata with a new endpoint.

lisa_ng: Support note: escalating to P1 because production login blocked, cc-ing eng-sre for logs access. support-bot: escalating ticket STR-1824 to eng-security (P1).

support-bot: Ticket STR-1824 summary: SSO failures after IdP cert rotation. Errors: InvalidSignature, Destination mismatch. Org: acme-corp. Linked thread: #support.

jack.wong: For the SAMLResponse decode you can do this locally to check the Assertion and Signature:
```bash
# decode base64 saml response
echo '<BASE64>' | base64 --decode | xmllint --format -
# or python quick decode
python - <<'PY'
import base64,sys
s = base64.b64decode(sys.stdin.read())
print(s.decode('utf-8'))
PY
```
Look for <Assertion> Issuer, Signature, SubjectConfirmationData Recipient attribute — the Recipient must match our ACS URL exactly.

acme-admin: Decoded Assertion includes Recipient="https://console.redwoodinference.com/saml/consume". Signature contains Cert: "MIIC...REDACTED...AB" (looks same as metadata). We also tried re-uploading metadata after rotation; still fails.

samir.patel: Could be that the cert got wrapped with extra whitespace/newlines when pasted into the IdP UI. Also run this to fingerprint:
```bash
# save cert PEM to idp_cert.pem then:
openssl x509 -in idp_cert.pem -noout -sha1 -fingerprint -inform PEM
```
Post the fingerprint here (format: SHA1 Fingerprint=XX:YY:...). We'll compare to the fingerprint in our logs.

acme-admin: Fingerprint reported by openssl: SHA1 Fingerprint=AA:BB:CC:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99:00:AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00

jack.wong: Our logs show SAML signature verification failed. Expected IdP fingerprint on record: AA:BB:CC:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99:00:AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00 — that matches their cert. So signature mismatch might be due to algorithm mismatch (IdP signed with SHA256 but SP expects SHA1 signature). We recently tightened allowed algorithms to disallow SHA1 in some flows. Did you see any alg warnings?

acme-admin: Browser console had a warning: "SAML signature uses SHA1-SignedXml" but server error was InvalidSignature. We didn't change signing algorithm during rotation; vendor says they use RSA-SHA256 by default.

maria.chen: Good catch. Jack, can we check validation policy for this org — maybe they landed on legacy SHA1 policy after rotation? Also check if the cert the vendor provided is the correct signing cert vs encryption cert (some vendors publish both). If our validator picked the encryption cert, signature would fail.

samir.patel: I'll pull the SAML debug trace from our SP logs for STR-1824 and check which certificate (kid/fingerprint) we attempted to use. Give me 20 mins.

(20 minutes later)

samir.patel: From SP logs: Received SAMLResponse signed by fingerprint AA:BB:CC:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99:00:AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00; our validator attempted to verify using the cert in metadata, but verification failed with error: "signature verification error: incorrect padding" — which usually means the cert in metadata is not the same bytes (linebreaks or header/footer altered) OR the IdP is signing with a different key (rotate published but didn't actually use it). Also saw Destination mismatch warning earlier.

jack.wong: Two remediation paths: 1) Ask IdP admin to re-export metadata directly (download file, don't copy/paste) and re-upload to Redwood console; 2) Add the alternate ACS URL (https://console.redwoodinference.com/saml/consume) as a valid Recipient on our side temporarily so their current config works while they correct metadata. Maria — can support add alternate ACS for org?

maria.chen: We can add a temporary ACS alias per-org via the admin UI; documenting caution in the ticket. acme-admin — do you want us to add the alias while you confirm fresh metadata from IdP?

acme-admin: Yes please — add the alias so users can sign in ASAP. We'll also request the IdP to re-export metadata and confirm they are signing with the new cert.

support-bot: Added ACS alias https://console.redwoodinference.com/saml/consume for org acme-corp (temporary). Flagged to remove after 72h.

acme-admin: After alias added, I can confirm several users could sign in. We still want to resolve the cert/signature mismatch permanently.

samir.patel: Follow-up actions: 1) acme admin to upload the downloaded metadata XML here once the IdP confirms rotation complete. 2) We'll compare certificate bytes and fingerprint; if mismatch persists, ask IdP to publish signing key only and ensure no line-wrapping. 3) We'll remove ACS alias after they confirm metadata.

jack.wong: Also logging a small product task for us to improve metadata upload validation to detect common whitespace/truncation issues (ENG-SSO-473).

maria.chen: Marking ticket STR-1824 as P1 - mitigated (ACS alias), pending permanent fix. We'll keep this thread updated. :white_check_mark:

acme-admin: Thanks all — appreciate the quick help. I'll paste the official metadata file here once we get it from the IdP.

(17:46) samir.patel: noted — will monitor logs for any further InvalidSignature events and confirm when we remove the alias.

(17:59) support-bot: STR-1824 updated: ACS alias enabled, customer authenticated via alias, awaiting metadata re-upload. Scheduled alias removal in 72h unless customer confirms fixed earlier.
